title: Failure Cartography: Adaptive Tracehook Sampling & SLA Exposure Gauges
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current error dashboards and tracing hooks surface high-level counts (timeouts, overloads, gRPC/HTTP codes) but do not show how SLO exposure accumulates across correlated failure slices. This makes it hard for oncall and SREs to prioritize fixes when a single upstream change causes broad SLO drift across many customers and routes.

Goal: Build a Failure Cartography layer that combines adaptive tracehook sampling, slice-driven ingestion, and SLA exposure gauges so we can: 1) visualize which failure slices (route x model x region x error-type) contribute most to SLO erosion, 2) reduce storage and query costs by sampling traces more intelligently, and 3) provide action-friendly drilldowns for triage.

Scope:
- Add a tracehook sampling policy that increases sampling for slices with rising error rate or SLO burn (slice-driven sampling).
- Emit a compact "failure tile" metric per request (immutable) capturing key enums: error_class (timeout|overload|model_error|proto_error|http_4xx|http_5xx), route_id, model_variant, region, plan_tier, latency_bucket.
- New Grafana/Loki dashboards: SLA Exposure Gauges (per-tenant and per-route), Failure Cartography heatmap (slice prominence over time), and an Action Panel linking to traces/PRs/incident docs.
- Backfill plan: run the failure-tile generator for 7 days in parallel with production to validate cardinality and cost before full switch.

Non-Goals: building a full incident responder; changing inference routing or automatic rollbacks in this ticket.

Implementation notes:
- Use the existing tracehook ingestion path but add a lightweight pre-filter that computes the failure tile and increments counters in a new TSDB namespace (slo_exposure.failure_tiles).
- Sampling policy is rules-based with thresholds: if slice error_rate > 0.5% or slice_slo_burn > 0.2% for 5m window, sample at 100 req/min for that slice for next 10m; otherwise fall back to baseline reservoir sampling (1%).
- Persist slice metadata to a small Redis-like store for fast lookups (TTL 24h) to avoid repeated tag hashing in hot paths.
- Dashboard queries will aggregate the slo_exposure namespace by top-N slices per window and compute cumulative SLO burn contribution.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Failure tiles emitted for >=99.5% of error and SLO-burned requests in the canary region during the 7-day backfill.
- Sampling policy triggers observed in traces and increases trace capture for prioritized slices by >=10x vs baseline during injected fault tests.
- New dashboards load within 2s for 30-day overview panel and show top 25 contributing slices.
- Documented rollout checklist and rollback plan in Confluence with cost estimate and cardinality report.
acceptance_criteria: Emit failure_tile metric for errors and SLO-burned requests with <0.5% loss during canary backfill
Adaptive sampling policy increases trace capture >=10x for targeted slices during fault injection
SLA Exposure Gauge dashboards show cumulative SLO contribution and top-25 slices within 2s query latency
Confluence runbook with cost/cardinality analysis and rollback steps published
Unit and integration tests for failure_tile generator and sampling policy merged to main
comments: 2026-03-05 — Asha: Kickoff: scoped initial prototype for tracehook pre-filter + failure_tile schema. Agreed to keep failure_tile compact to control cardinality.

2026-03-07 — Liam: Prototype pushed to feature branch. failure_tile schema: [error_class, route_id, model_variant, region, plan_tier, latency_bucket, request_size_bin]. PR: github.com/redwood/tracehooks/pull/1542
2026-03-09 — Security review (preliminary): no PII in failure_tile; plan_tier is allowed. Security requested explicit KMS usage for the Redis metadata store credentials.
2026-03-10 — SRE sync: suggested a 1-hour cool-down for sampling toggles to avoid oscillation. Decided to implement exponential backoff on sampling reversion.

2026-03-12 — Engineering review: changed default baseline sampling to 0.5% (was 1%) to offset expected increase in sampled traces once slice-based rules hit. Updated PR: github.com/redwood/tracehooks/pull/1569

2026-03-13 — QA: injected synthetic timeout across model-variant 'redwood-7B-v2' in eu-west to validate policy. Observed 12x increase in trace capture for that slice in staging. Link to dashboard: grafana.redwood/team/slo-exposure?panelId=9
2026-03-14 — Liam: canary backfill scheduled for eu-west on 2026-03-15. Cost estimate placed in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Failure+Cartography+Cost+Estimate
implementation_steps: Design failure_tile schema and validate cardinality with historical logs (2 days)
Implement tracehook pre-filter and failure_tile emitter (4 days)
Add sampling policy evaluator and Redis metadata cache (3 days)
Create slo_exposure TSDB namespace and Grafana dashboards (3 days)
Deploy canary backfill for 7 days in eu-west; collect cardinality and cost metrics (7 days)
Post-mortem and full rollout plan; enable on production after cost acceptance
risks_and_mitigations: Cardinality explosion — mitigation: enforce strict enum sets and coarse bucketization for model_variant and route_id; gate with canary backfill
Increased ingestion costs — mitigation: lower baseline sampling and apply slice-level caps; run 7-day cost forecast before full rollout
Oscillating sampling decisions — mitigation: add cool-down and exponential backoff on sampling toggles
Missing context for triage — mitigation: include direct links to full trace and recent related PRs in the dashboard action panel
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to the observability ingestion and visualization layer. Any automatic routing/fallback changes must be handled in a follow-up ticket.
If successful, this design can be extended to quota-aware sampling for Dedicated customers in Private deployments (separate project)
